desc: Read N, arrays A and B, K, and queries.
Collect all distinct X and Y values from queries. Sort them.
Coordinate compress all values in A and B.
Build Fenwick trees for A and B that can answer: for a given prefix (1..X) and value v, count and sum of elements ≤ v.

Process queries offline: for each distinct X, maintain a sorted list of distinct values in A[1..X] (using a dictionary for counts and a sorted list of keys). Insertion of new values is O(log D) using bisect. Do the same for B and distinct Y.

For each query (X,Y), iterate over the distinct values in the prefix with fewer distinct values (say A[1..X] if it has fewer distinct values than B[1..Y]), and for each distinct value v with count c, query the B Fenwick tree for prefix Y to get count_le and sum_le of B elements ≤ v. Accumulate c * (v * count_le - sum_le). Then compute S using the formula.
Handle the case where X or Y is 0? Not needed as per constraints.
Test the solution with the provided sample inputs to ensure correctness.
Profile with maximum constraints to identify bottlenecks.
Optimize if needed: consider using array module for Fenwick tree, or segment tree with sorted lists for O(log N) query of sorted prefixes.
Test with edge cases: large values, duplicate values, maximum N and K.
